subject: CloudWard head-to-head evaluation: recap + next-test handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudward.com>, Infra Team <infra@cloudward.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Nov 2029 18:12:00 -0800
Subject: CloudWard head-to-head evaluation: recap + next-test handoff

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and a proposal for the next test steps so we can align on a clean A/B that answers p95/p99 and sustained tokens/sec.

Call highlights (short):
- Goal: validate real app SLOs for the customer-facing chat feature (target: p95 < 80ms, p99 < 260ms, sustained tokens/sec >= 4k at 50 concurrent sessions).
- Current infra: you mentioned spanning two regions with HyperscaleA managed clusters and a custom batching layer on Triton.
- Key unknowns we want to control: sequence length distribution (75th/95th tokens), batching config, quantization (fp16 vs int8) and warm vs cold KV-cache behavior.

Proposed A/B plan (attached as proposed-ab-plan.md):
1) Phase A - microbench: identical sample payloads, single-request latency runs to measure cold vs warm; measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
2) Phase B - sustained QPS: run 10m windows at target QPS (ramp 5min) to surface microbursts and batching artifacts.
3) Phase C - production-like: replay 1hr of anonymized traces (only if you can provide), capture tail-latency distributions and variance across regions.

Success gating (suggested):
- p95 and p99 within target on your production traces OR a clear mitigation path (KV-cache, dynamic batching) that keeps average cost within 20% of baseline.
- No catastrophic tail (>1s p99) during 10m sustained runs.

What we need from CloudWard to execute:
- Representative JSON payloads for 50/75/95 token buckets (anonymized)
- Target concurrency / QPS targets for each phase
- Confirmation if you want Redwood-hosted runs (we provide A100/80GB) or to run Redwood Dedicated in your VPC (we can coordinate infra).

Attachments: headtohead-summary-annotated.png (visual summary), proposed-ab-plan.md (test matrix).

Next steps: if you confirm the sample payloads + target windows, we can run Phase A on Monday and share a CSV of p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.ai]

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudward.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Infra Team <infra@cloudward.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Dec 2029 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudWard head-to-head evaluation: recap + next-test handoff

Appreciate the clear write-up, Jordan. A few clarifications before we share test artifacts: 

- We can share anonymized payloads (75/150/350 token buckets) but need an NDA addendum for the replay harness (contains internal request IDs).
- For Phase A/B we care most about p99 on 350-token requests (that’s what our long-form assistant uses).
- Our current baseline: HyperscaleA (T4 fleet via Triton) yields ~p95=95-120ms, p99=340-420ms on 350-token sequences at 50 conc. We want to know whether Redwood’s hosting or your Dedicated flavor closes that gap with consistent tails.

Couple asks: can you include region-specific runs? EU traffic is sensitive so we’d like an EU region comparison too. Also please include a lightweight cost estimate (cost per 1M generated tokens) for each config you run.

If you can send the NDA link, infra will upload a zipped sample set this afternoon. Preferred test window: Dec 5-6.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudWard
samira.k@cloudward.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudward.com>, Infra Team <infra@cloudward.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Dec 2029 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudWard head-to-head evaluation: recap + next-test handoff

Thanks — NDA link below, and attaching an initial microbench CSV so you can see our measurement format.

NDA: https://drive.google.com/redwood/nda/cloudward-addendum
Attached: redwood-initial-microbench.csv, headtohead-summary-annotated.png

Quick notes on the CSV and how we interpret:
- redwood-initial-microbench.csv contains three runs: Redwood-hosted (A100-80GB, fp16), Redwood-dedicated-sim (A100-equivalent, int8), and HyperscaleA reference (T4 via Triton). Columns: seq_len, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec.
- High level from our informal microbench (same sample payloads you described):
  * Redwood-hosted (A100 fp16): seq=350 => p95 ~48ms, p99 ~220ms, tokens/sec ~6.4k
  * Redwood-dedicated-sim (A100 int8 path): seq=350 => p95 ~42ms, p99 ~198ms, tokens/sec ~7.1k
  * HyperscaleA (T4 Triton): seq=350 => p95 ~110ms, p99 ~390ms, tokens/sec ~3.9k
- Important caveats: our int8 path requires a per-model validation step; small accuracy delta observed on a narrow set of prompts (we log perplexity/qa-delta in the CSV). Batching and KV cache warm-up change the tail substantially — cold-start p99s can spike >600ms on long sequences.

Proposed next-tests (concrete):
1) Phase A (Dec 5 AM): Redwood-hosted vs HyperscaleA single-instance cold->warm microbench. 2 runs per config, capture raw logs.
2) Phase B (Dec 5 PM): sustained 10m window at your 50-conc workload; include a microburst spike (2x QPS for 30s) near the 5-minute mark.
3) Phase C (Dec 6): optional region-run (EU) if you provide EU sample set.

Cost estimate (very rough, ballpark): Redwood-hosted A100 fp16 ~ $12 / 1M tokens; Dedicated int8 path ~ $9 / 1M tokens (depends on utilization). We’ll produce a formal quote after we know run durations.

If that schedule looks good we’ll reserve capacity and share exact run IDs + log collection hooks.

-Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Dec 2029 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: CloudWard head-to-head evaluation: recap + next-test handoff

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding the CloudWard thread and initial microbench. Actions for us before Dec 5 run: 

- Marissa: please reserve Redwood-hosted A100 capacity Dec 5 AM (slot for 2x 30m runs). Prepare the run spec to match the attached CSV payload format and include a cold-start full-kv-cache flush between the two runs.
- Karthik: can you assemble a canary config that mirrors HyperscaleA batching (Triton-like small-batch aggressiveness) so we test identical batching heuristics? Also add GPU-side metrics (SM utilization, mem-copy stall) to the logs.
- Both: add a simple accuracy check (top-k token overlap) for the int8 path and flag if QA-delta > 1.5% — we’ll present that to Samira as an accuracy-risk note.

I’ll coordinate the Run IDs and log hooks; goal is to hand the CSVs and raw logs back to CloudWard within 4 hours of each run.

Thanks — Jordan
